newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy CPI improving but Sept data bad - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italy CPI improving but Sept data bad - Fazio.

text.p: Italian inflation is falling but the September data was not good, Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio told a parliamentary commission on Thursday.
"The June, July and August data were all very good, the September figures were not good...We are improving," Fazio said, replying to a question.
"Is it possible that the past three figures were accidental? I hope not," Fazio said.
Inflation has fallen steadily since the start of the year, but the decline was halted last month when inflation came in unchanged from August's levels at 3.4 percent year-on-year.
Fazio repeated that the Bank of Italy's monetary policy "is aimed at lowering the inflation rate to enable a permanent lowering of structural interest rates."
Fazio indicated last month that a further rate cut was dependent on inflation falling under three percent.
The discount rate was cut to 8.25 percent from nine percent in July. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
